supersedes.note: This proposal supersedes NOTHING until a separate owner approval record naming this file's SHA-256 exists. F6_FINAL_DEV_DECISION_RULE_V1 and the F9 result DEV_NOT_READY_FOR_HOLDOUT remain the operative, immutable history.

candidateIndependence.thresholdsDerivedFrom: stated principles and pre-existing owner-approved constants, never from any candidate's observed score
candidateIndependence.statement: No rule, threshold, floor, denominator or split in this document was selected by computing what would make V1-V6 pass. Historical results were used ONLY to diagnose properties of the METHOD (denominator size, run-to-run variance, clustering, adaptive reuse), as Phase 2B-2D's own revision instruction permits.

diagnosis.summary: The frozen method cannot establish any property it claims to gate, because every gate's threshold requires more observations than its denominator supplies. This is arithmetic, it is independent of any candidate, and it was true for V1 as it is for V6.

d1_noGateIsCertifiable.claim: At the DEVELOPMENT denominators, NO frozen gate is established even by a flawless candidate (zero observed errors), at 95% one-sided exact (Clopper-Pearson) confidence.
d1_noGateIsCertifiable.consequence: Passing such a gate is not evidence that the threshold holds, and failing it is not evidence that it does not. The gate is unfalsifiable at its own denominator.

d2_twoGatesAreSilentlyZeroTolerance.claim: minUnitPageRecall >= 0.95 over 14 items and minSchemaValidSpanVerifiedRate >= 0.99 over 49 items tolerate ZERO errors. 13/14 = 0.9286 and 48/49 = 0.9796 both fail. The two-decimal thresholds imply a tolerance the denominators do not provide.

d3_compoundRuleStringencyWasNeverCompute.claim: A candidate whose TRUE per-item recall is exactly the 0.95 the gate names passes a zero-miss 14-item recall gate with probability 0.95^14 = 0.4877, and therefore passes all five replicates with probability 0.0276.
d3_compoundRuleStringencyWasNeverCompute.consequence: The frozen 5/5-must-pass rule rejects a threshold-compliant candidate about 97 times in 100. To pass with probability 0.8 a candidate needs true per-item recall >= 0.99682 - the rule demands ~99.7% while claiming to demand 95%.
d3_compoundRuleStringencyWasNeverCompute.recordedButUnanswered: F0U section 11 named this exact failure mode ('may be too strict for a genuinely marginal-but-real improvement to ever clear'). The F2 freeze adopted pass-every-replication without answering it; its entire recorded justification is that the rule is 'strictly stronger' than the prior single-run rule.
d3_compoundRuleStringencyWasNeverCompute.classification: FACT (arithmetic) + NOT RECOVERABLE (the selection rationale is absent from the repository)

d4_replicatesDoNotAddItemEvidence.claim: The N=5 replicates resample stochastic model noise over a FIXED 49 items. They do not enlarge the item sample: item-level uncertainty is still governed by 14 gold UNIT_PAGE items, not 70.
d4_replicatesDoNotAddItemEvidence.consequence: The method uses replication as if it were extra evidence while its decision rule compounds replicate noise multiplicatively. Replication measures STABILITY; it cannot certify ACCURACY. The frozen rule conflates the two.

d5_organisationClusteringIsUnrecorded.claim: The 49 DEVELOPMENT items come from 12 organisations (3-5 items each). The 14 gold UNIT_PAGE items occupy only 9 of those 12, and one organisation carries 4 of 14 (28.6%). Three organisations contribute zero positives.
d5_organisationClusteringIsUnrecorded.recordedGap: F0U section 9 records BATCH-level non-independence (12 batches of ~4 documents, one provider call per batch) but NO document anywhere records ORGANISATION-level clustering.
d5_organisationClusteringIsUnrecorded.worse: DEVELOPMENT and HOLDOUT are deliberately NOT organisation-disjoint - PHASE_2B_2D_GOLD_CORPUS_PROTOCOL.md section 17: 'every organisation contributes to both sides'. HOLDOUT therefore tests generalisation to NEW PAGES OF KNOWN ORGANISATIONS, never to new organisations.
d5_organisationClusteringIsUnrecorded.whyItMatters: The production question is whether an ORGANISATION can be qualified. The organisation is the unit the estimate must generalise over, and it is neither the sampling unit nor the inference unit today.
d5_organisationClusteringIsUnrecorded.classification: FACT (measured) + NOT RECOVERABLE (never recorded as a limitation)

d6_adaptiveReuseIsRealAndUnmitigated.recorded: F0U section 12: 'Repeated inspection of the same 49 labelled DEVELOPMENT items across D1->D2->D3->E1 ... creates a real, structural risk of increasingly item-specific tuning - a prompt that has been iteratively adjusted against the same 49 answers stops being evidence about the underlying task and starts being evidence about those 49 answers specifically.'
d6_adaptiveReuseIsRealAndUnmitigated.cap: F0U section 12 recommended that no further semantic iteration (a hypothetical V6) be attempted against the same 49-item fixture before the replication study completed.
d6_adaptiveReuseIsRealAndUnmitigated.whatHappened: V6 is the fifth successive prompt edit diagnosed against the same 49 labels, and its rules R1/R2/R3 were designed by inspecting the serialized payloads of seven named DEVELOPMENT items including all three critical ones.
d6_adaptiveReuseIsRealAndUnmitigated.gap: The F0U section 12 caveat and its iteration cap entered NO freeze. A repository-wide search for 'overfit' across docs/evaluation/*.json returns zero hits.
d6_adaptiveReuseIsRealAndUnmitigated.consequence: There is no untouched confirmation split anywhere between DEVELOPMENT and the one-shot HOLDOUT.

consequences: Three of four unit_type classes are SINGLETONS in DEVELOPMENT; unit_type accuracy is effectively a measurement of one class.
The NO axis class has a structurally EMPTY gold denominator, so any NO-accuracy metric is permanently vacuous.
EN (7) sits below MIN_SUBGROUP_SIZE_FOR_GATING (20) and can never fail a gate; the 2D2C six-gate contract has no subgroup gate at all.

The production distribution is the ECHE register (6,139 source rows, all Erasmus countries). No document in the repository claims this corpus represents it, and the design documents repeatedly record the opposite as a KNOWN LIMITATION.

d8_holdoutMultiplicityIsUncontrolled.claim: HOLDOUT discipline is 'scored once per frozen candidate', with no recorded limit on the number of candidates. An unbounded sequence of one-shot scorings has an uncontrolled family-wise error rate.
d8_holdoutMultiplicityIsUncontrolled.classification: METHODOLOGICAL ASSUMPTION (that one-shot-per-candidate preserves HOLDOUT integrity across unboundedly many candidates) - never stated, never bounded.

d9_theEvidenceBaseCannotBeResplitToFixTh.claim: The ENTIRE 160-item candidate pool holds only 28 proposed UNIT_PAGE items (22 already consumed by the 72-item acceptance corpus; 6 remain in the unused 88-item residual).
d9_theEvidenceBaseCannotBeResplitToFixTh.consequence: The maximum gold UNIT_PAGE denominator obtainable from all captured evidence, under every possible re-split, is 28 - against the 59 needed to certify 0.95 with a flawless run. No re-partition of existing evidence can make the recall gate certifiable. NEW ACQUISITION IS MANDATORY.
d9_theEvidenceBaseCannotBeResplitToFixTh.alsoMeasured: The working database nwf_pe is empty (all orgunit_* tables, organisations and website_claims at 0 rows), so the cohort that produced the pool no longer exists outside the committed fixtures.

d10_sixGatesIsAmbiguousInTheFrozenBytes.claim: The F2 freeze's sixFrozenDevGates object carries ELEVEN keys; the F6 freeze's carries exactly six. The decision rule in both enumerates only 'the six frozen DEV gates'.
d10_sixGatesIsAmbiguousInTheFrozenBytes.consequence: Whether isolation violations, evidence-span verification, unitName verification and the language-subgroup rules are GATES or REPORTING is not decidable from the frozen bytes.

d11_twoLiveDenominatorConventionsDisagre.claim: metrics.ts computes unit_type accuracy over the intersection (gold UNIT_PAGE AND model UNIT_PAGE); the 2D2C scorer computes it strictly over gold UNIT_PAGE (denominator 14). maxNeedsReviewRate likewise differs (over valid results vs over all 49).
d11_twoLiveDenominatorConventionsDisagre.consequence: Two different numbers can both be called 'the unit_type gate'. A revision must name one.

d12_labelQualityIsUnmeasured.claim: Of the 49 DEVELOPMENT labels, 26 are OWNER-ratified (ratification of editorially-drafted proposals, not independent labelling) and 23 were confirmed with no owner review at all.
d12_labelQualityIsUnmeasured.measured: There is ZERO inter-rater measurement anywhere in the repository: no second annotator, no percent agreement, no Cohen's kappa. The only blinded review that exists is the G1 packet, which covered exactly ONE item.
d12_labelQualityIsUnmeasured.consequence: Gold label error is not merely unbounded, it is unmeasured - and at a recall denominator of 14 a single mislabelled item moves the metric by 7.1 points.
d12_labelQualityIsUnmeasured.classification: FACT (measured) + NOT RECOVERABLE (no agreement statistic was ever computed)

designPrinciples: P1. A gate must be FEASIBLE before it is frozen. Pre-registration must prove that some attainable observation certifies it. A gate whose certification needs more trials than the split supplies is forbidden.

P2. Separate the three questions the frozen rule conflates: QUALITY (is the true rate above the bar?), STABILITY (is behaviour reproducible?), INTEGRITY (was the run structurally sound?). Each gets its own instrument.
P3. The generalisation unit is the ORGANISATION, because the product qualifies organisations. Splits are organisation-disjoint and uncertainty is computed with the organisation as the cluster.
P4. Replication measures stability, never accuracy. Replicates may not be pooled as though they were independent items.
P5. Keep the substantive quality bar; add a certified floor beneath it. The point estimate preserves the ambition; the lower confidence bound proves it was not luck.
P6. Invent no uncalibrated constant. Where a bound is needed, reuse an existing owner-approved constant or label the new one a MECHANICAL SAFETY BOUND, NOT A CALIBRATED VALUE.
P7. Infrastructure failure is not a semantic property of the candidate, and must not be scored as one.
P8. Every number in a decision must be recomputable from committed integers by an independent implementation.

proposedSplits.change: THREE organisation-disjoint splits replace the current two page-level splits.
proposedSplits.rationale: The current split assigns pages within each organisation to both sides, so no split measures generalisation to an unseen organisation. It also leaves no untouched confirmation set between an endlessly-iterated DEVELOPMENT and a one-shot HOLDOUT.

splits.name: DEV_TRAIN
splits.promptAuthorsMayInspect: everything - items, documents, gold labels, rationales, full model outputs, per-item results
splits.purpose: candidate design and diagnosis; unlimited iteration

splits.name: DEV_CONFIRM
splits.promptAuthorsMayInspect: NOTHING - not items, not documents, not labels, not per-item results, not aggregate metrics before the scoring is frozen
splits.burnRule: Any inspection of a DEV_CONFIRM item by a prompt author permanently moves that item to DEV_TRAIN and it must be replaced from reserve before the next scoring.
splits.scoringBudget: one scoring per frozen candidate; at most 5 candidates per methodology epoch

splits.name: HOLDOUT
splits.purpose: the single confirmatory test before Phase 2E eligibility
splits.accessRule: owner-authorised, one-shot per frozen candidate, only after a DEV_CONFIRM pass
splits.multiplicityNote: At most 3 candidates may EVER be scored against one HOLDOUT instance. At 3 scorings the Bonferroni family-wise error rate is at most 0.143 at alpha 0.05; the budget exists so that number is bounded and recorded rather than unbounded and hidden. A fourth candidate requires a NEW holdout drawn from organisations never used before.

proposedSplits.disjointness: ORGANISATION-DISJOINT. No organisation may contribute items to more than one split. This is a deliberate reversal of GOLD_CORPUS_PROTOCOL section 17 ('every organisation contributes to both sides') and is the single most important structural change proposed here.
proposedSplits.assignmentRule: Organisations are ordered by a content-derived key (sha256 of eche_row_key) ascending and assigned round-robin to DEV_TRAIN, DEV_CONFIRM, HOLDOUT under a frozen pattern, so assignment cannot correlate with any label, difficulty judgement or model result.

proposedAcceptanceRule.appliesTo: one FROZEN candidate evaluated on one named split with R replicates

replicates.justification: R >= 3 is the minimum that can separate a STABLE error (wrong in every replicate) from an INTERMITTENT one; R = 5 gives a majority with margin and a per-item propensity on a 6-point grid. R is NOT a power parameter and does not enlarge the item sample.
replicates.classification: RECORDED DESIGN DECISION with a stated purpose. This is a change from the frozen N=5, whose recorded justification (F0U section 5) was a judgement anchored on an owner default for a two-arm DIAGNOSTIC study, transferred unexamined to a one-arm ACCEPTANCE study.

stage0_admissibility.note: INADMISSIBLE is not REJECT. It says the study did not measure the candidate, so nothing may be concluded about it in either direction.
conditions: A0.1 every planned evaluation in every replicate produced an observed item result; no imputation, no substitution, no extrapolation from an observed prefix
A0.2 the replicate count equals the frozen R exactly; no replicate replaced, discarded or rerun
A0.3 every provider call used the approved Claude Max subscription path (ADR 0010) through the Agent SDK; zero Console-API-key, PAYG, Bedrock, Vertex or other provider/auth path
A0.4 tool, MCP, browser and isolation violations across all attempts: 0
A0.5 no gold label was loaded by, or reachable from, the inference path
A0.6 the candidate (prompt version, output schema version, request configuration) was hashed and committed before the first provider request, and unchanged after it
A0.7 every evaluated goldId belongs to the declared split, and the split's organisation-disjointness holds
A0.8 non-terminal infrastructure failures per replicate do not exceed MAX_NON_TERMINAL_TIMEOUTS_PER_REPLICATE (2); at the ceiling the STUDY is INADMISSIBLE rather than silently partial

stage1_integrityVetoes.note: These are zero-tolerance by nature, and are stated as vetoes rather than as rate gates. minSchemaValidSpanVerifiedRate >= 0.99 was ALREADY a zero-tolerance gate at n=49; naming it a veto states the same requirement honestly and removes a threshold that would need n=299 to certify.

vetoes.rule: count of items whose structured output is still invalid after the one bounded ADR 0011 repair round, summed over all replicates, must be 0
count of unverifiable evidence spans, and of non-null unitName values that do not verify against the document, summed over all replicates, must be 0
count of ORGANISATIONS that have at least one gold UNIT_PAGE item but for which the candidate recalls no UNIT_PAGE at all in at least ceil(R/2) replicates must be 0
vetoes.rationale: This is the downstream catastrophe the product actually cannot absorb: an organisation with no recalled unit page is silently dropped from the pipeline and is unrecoverable later. A page-level miss whose sibling page is recalled is recoverable. No frozen gate expresses this, because no frozen metric has an organisation denominator.
vetoes.classification: NEW. Derived from the downstream failure mode, not from any candidate's behaviour.

stage2_quality.estimand: the candidate's true per-item correctness rate over the ORGANISATION population from which the split's organisations were drawn
procedure: Q2.1 for each item i, compute the propensity p_i = (number of replicates in which item i was answered correctly for this metric) / R
Q2.2 group items by organisation; each organisation is one cluster
Q2.3 compute the one-sided 95% lower confidence bound by resampling WHOLE ORGANISATIONS with replacement (clusterBootstrapLowerBound, alpha 0.05, resamples 20000, seed frozen in the study freeze)
Q2.4 compute the exact Clopper-Pearson one-sided 95% lower bound over the item-majority outcomes as a conservative cross-check, and REPORT BOTH; the clustered bound is the binding one
Q2.5 report the raw numerator/denominator for every metric, never a bare percentage

gates.denominator: gold UNIT_PAGE items in the split
items answered UNIT_PAGE by a validator-accepted result
gates.samplingCaveat: Precision depends on class prevalence. It MUST be estimated on a prevalence-faithful sample (SET_P below), never on the positive-enriched recall sample, or it is inflated by construction.

gates.denominator: items whose GOLD verdict is UNIT_PAGE (the 2D2C convention, adopted explicitly; see d11)
gates.additionalRequirement: at least 2 gold items in each unit_type class that is gated; a class with fewer is REPORTED and explicitly NOT GATED, never silently folded into the aggregate

gates.denominator: gold hard negatives in the split

floorDerivation.source: MAX_SUBGROUP_SHORTFALL in src/orgunits/classify/evaluation/protocol.ts - the repository's OWN already-frozen, owner-approved notion of how far below a gate is still not catastrophic.
floorDerivation.whyThisMatters: Reusing an existing approved constant means the floor is not a new calibration decision made by this task, and it is provably not chosen to make any candidate pass. Every pointEstimateTarget is IDENTICAL to the currently-frozen threshold: the substantive quality bar is unchanged, and a certified floor is added beneath it.

stage3_stability.rule: S3.1 no single replicate's point estimate for any gated metric may fall below that metric's certifiedFloor (or above its certifiedCeiling).
stage3_stability.reportingRequirement: S3.2 the full per-replicate distribution of every gated metric is reported, including the range (max - min). A range above 0.10 on any gated metric must be labelled INSTABILITY_OBSERVED in the report.
stage3_stability.whyNoDispersionThreshold: S3.2 is REPORTING, not a gate, because no measurement in this repository calibrates a dispersion tolerance, and inventing one would repeat the mistake migration 0008 corrected. Instability is already penalised twice over: an unstable candidate breaches the S3.1 floor on its worst replicate, and its per-item propensities fall, which lowers the Stage 2 clustered bound.
stage3_stability.replaces: the frozen 'each of the 5/5 replicates individually passes every one of the six frozen DEV gates', which demands per-replicate near-certainty (see d3) and rejects a threshold-compliant candidate ~97% of the time
stage3_stability.lineage: This is the shape F0U section 11 tabulated as 'median-metric-plus-no-catastrophic-replicate', with the clustered lower confidence bound in place of the median - which removes the objection F0U itself raised against that option ('requires picking a floor value, which is itself a new calibration decision'), because the floor is now derived from an existing approved constant.

stage4_aggregation.rule: ACCEPT if and only if stage 0, stage 1, stage 2 and stage 3 all hold. Otherwise REJECT (or INADMISSIBLE per stage 0).
stage4_aggregation.noPooling: results from different splits, different methodology epochs or different reliability-semantics versions are never pooled
stage4_aggregation.vacuousGateIsReportedAndBlocks: a gate whose denominator is 0 is INADMISSIBLE for that metric, never a pass - a change from the frozen metrics.ts behaviour, where a vacuous gate returns pass: true

missingnessAndRetrySemantics.infrastructureInvalid: A non-terminal provider TIMEOUT or transport failure is INFRASTRUCTURE, not a semantic property of the candidate (P7). Its items are excluded from SEMANTIC denominators, reported separately with their exact count, and capped by A0.8.
missingnessAndRetrySemantics.changeFromFrozen: The frozen semantics score an infrastructure-caused INVALID item as a strict semantic miss against recall and hard-negative rejection. That makes the gate partly a measurement of the host and the network.
missingnessAndRetrySemantics.assumptionStated: This exclusion is unbiased only if infrastructure failure is independent of item difficulty. That is plausible for a transport timeout but is UNMEASURED, and is recorded here as a METHODOLOGICAL ASSUMPTION rather than a fact.
missingnessAndRetrySemantics.candidateInvalid: A validator rejection surviving the one bounded repair round is a genuine candidate output failure and triggers veto V1.1.
missingnessAndRetrySemantics.retry: no retry of a completed evaluation; no replacement of a replicate; no rerun of a failed replicate
missingnessAndRetrySemantics.terminalFailure: a replicate reaching a terminal failure makes the STUDY INADMISSIBLE; it is never scored as a partial result

modelSelection.reason: The production model is fixed by owner product decision (Claude Sonnet 5). This rule accepts or rejects a CANDIDATE CONFIGURATION, it does not compare models.
modelSelection.ifSeveralCandidatesPass: select the highest clustered lower bound on unitPageRecall; ties broken by the precision lower bound, then by frozen candidate id ascending - deterministic, with no human discretion at the tie

feasibilityPrecondition.rule: A study freeze is INVALID unless, for every gated metric, gateFeasibility(certifiedFloor, plannedDenominator).certifiableAtThisDenominator === true, AND the split has at least MIN_CLUSTERS organisations.
feasibilityPrecondition.minClustersClassification: MECHANICAL SAFETY BOUND, NOT A CALIBRATED VALUE. Percentile cluster-bootstrap intervals are unreliable with few clusters; 30 is a conventional floor, not a measurement from this project.
feasibilityPrecondition.whyThisIsTheKeyInnovation: This is the check the frozen methodology never had. It is computable BEFORE any candidate exists and BEFORE any inference, and every currently-frozen gate fails it at the current DEVELOPMENT denominators.

corpusDecision.question: Can the existing 49-item DEVELOPMENT corpus remain sufficient for future candidate selection?
reasons: R1. It cannot certify any gate (d1). 14 gold UNIT_PAGE against 59 needed for 0.95, or 19 for the proposed 0.85 floor with zero errors and 40 with two.
R2. It cannot be repaired by re-splitting: the whole 160-item pool holds 28 proposed UNIT_PAGE items (d9).
R3. It has 12 organisations against MIN_CLUSTERS 30, and the positives occupy only 9 of them (d5).
R4. It has been inspected across five successive prompt iterations, so it is no longer an unbiased estimate of anything (d6).
R5. Three of four unit_type classes are singletons and the NO axis class is structurally empty (d7).

roleOfTheExisting49Items.neverAgainUsedFor: any acceptance, readiness or promotion decision
roleOfTheExisting49Items.rationale: Its labels are already burned by five iterations of inspection, which is exactly what DEV_TRAIN is for. Discarding it would waste real adjudicated evidence; promoting it would launder adaptive reuse into a decision.
roleOfTheExisting49Items.residual88PoolItems: may be adjudicated and added to DEV_TRAIN without any new acquisition, but they add only 6 proposed UNIT_PAGE items and no new organisations, so they do not affect the corpus decision.

proposedNewEvidenceSet.name: orgunit-classifier-acceptance-v2 (PROPOSED - not built, not acquired, not authorised by this file)

twoSampleDesign.ration: Recall and precision need DIFFERENT samples. Recall is conditional on gold being positive, so positive enrichment is legitimate and efficient. Precision is conditional on the MODEL predicting positive, so it depends on prevalence and enrichment inflates it. One sample cannot serve both without reweighting.

SET_P.purpose: precision, needs-review rate, hard-negative rejection, schema validity - every prevalence-dependent quantity
SET_P.sampling: prevalence-faithful: exactly what production assembly would hand the classifier, with no class filtering

SET_R.sampling: positive-enriched: gold UNIT_PAGE pages located across many organisations
SET_R.enrichmentIsDeclared: the enrichment factor is recorded, and SET_R is NEVER used for precision or for any prevalence-dependent metric

targets.classDistribution: prevalence-faithful within SET_P; SET_R enriched to reach the recall denominator

proposedNewEvidenceSet.acquisitionSource: the Phase 2B-1e bounded discovery orchestrator, against organisations drawn from the ECHE register - the ONLY approved acquisition path
proposedNewEvidenceSet.samplingRule: organisations drawn by md5(eche_row_key) ascending rank within declared strata, the same content-derived, label-blind mechanism the original 15-organisation holdout used; the drawn list is committed BEFORE acquisition
proposedNewEvidenceSet.stratification: organisation-stratified and country-stratified. The current corpus is 100% FR; the production distribution is not. At minimum the new set must include organisations from more than one country, or the single-country limitation must be restated as binding on every conclusion drawn.
proposedNewEvidenceSet.deduplicationRule: content-hash dedupe as production performs it, plus a per-organisation cap so no organisation dominates a split
proposedNewEvidenceSet.clusteringTreatment: the organisation is the sampling unit, the split unit and the inference cluster
proposedNewEvidenceSet.provenanceAndHashing: every document keeps its own documentSha256; each split keeps a corpus content hash and a manifest; gold labels live in a split-scoped file so a sealed split's labels cannot be opened by reading a mixed file
proposedNewEvidenceSet.sealedFileDiscipline: DEV_CONFIRM and HOLDOUT labels MUST live in split-scoped files. The current mixed 72-record and 160-record files make it impossible to read development aggregates without opening bytes that also contain holdout rows.
proposedNewEvidenceSet.notAuthorisedHere: This task designs the protocol only. It collects nothing, labels nothing, and issues no institution request.

alternativesConsidered.option: A - build the new evidence set as specified
alternativesConsidered.validity: the only option under which a production-selection claim is defensible
alternativesConsidered.cost: a substantial bounded-acquisition and adjudication programme

alternativesConsidered.option: B - keep a small corpus and lower the certified floors until they are feasible
alternativesConsidered.validity: internally consistent but the certified floors fall so far (a 14-item denominator certifies at best 0.807) that the resulting guarantee is too weak to justify production promotion

alternativesConsidered.option: C - keep the current corpus and abandon certification, declaring the gates descriptive
alternativesConsidered.validity: honest, and it is what the status quo ACTUALLY is; but it means no evidence-based production-selection claim can ever be made from this corpus
alternativesConsidered.note: Named explicitly because the status quo is option C while presenting itself as a strict gate.

goldPolicy.objective: the minimum defensible process, given that label error is currently unmeasured (d12) and that one mislabelled item moves a 14-item metric by 7.1 points
whatNeedsNoHuman: every deterministic/provenance-derived field: goldId, documentSha256, split assignment, language stratum, discovery method, track membership, sparse/truncated flags
whatRequiresHumanConfirmation: unit_type on every gold UNIT_PAGE item
goldPolicy.whyFrozenProvenanceCannotAnswerThese: The deterministic signal layer cannot separate a UNIT from a DEGREE PROGRAMME - that separation is the entire reason the semantic classifier exists (ADR 0007). No deterministic rule can supply the label the classifier is being graded against.

dualBlindReview.scope: ALL gold UNIT_PAGE items (the rare, high-stakes, gate-carrying class) plus a random 15% sample of gold negatives
dualBlindReview.purposeOfTheNegativeSample: to MEASURE label error rate and inter-rater agreement, which have never been measured at all
dualBlindReview.estimatedItemsUnderDualReview: approximately 40 positives plus approximately 32 sampled negatives per confirmation split
dualBlindReview.disagreementResolution: only DISAGREEMENTS reach the owner for adjudication; at 90% agreement that is roughly 7 items per split
dualBlindReview.reported: percent agreement and Cohen's kappa, reported with the corpus and recomputed in CI
dualBlindReview.secondReviewerConstraint: The second reviewer must be a second HUMAN. No model output may define or confirm gold (existing rule, retained). If no second human is available, the corpus must record UNMEASURED_LABEL_ERROR as a stated limitation - never a fabricated agreement statistic.
dualBlindReview.classification: the owner-work-minimising design: full review of the small high-stakes class, sampling for the large low-stakes class, owner involvement only at disagreements

goldPolicy.blinding: reviewers see the frozen document, the rubric and the candidate label options, and never a model prediction, a metric value, a gate outcome or a threshold effect - the G1 packet's own design, generalised
goldPolicy.noFabrication: an item whose correct label cannot be determined from its own captured evidence is labelled NEEDS_REVIEW or excluded with its reason recorded; it is never guessed

holdoutPolicy.developmentIsFor: candidate design and diagnosis, without limit, on DEV_TRAIN only
holdoutPolicy.confirmationSplitIsFor: the DEV_READY decision - a sealed set the prompt author has never seen, which is what makes a DEV pass evidence rather than a memory of previous failures
holdoutPolicy.whenHoldoutMayFirstBeAccessed: only after (a) this methodology is owner-approved and frozen, (b) the new evidence set exists with its splits sealed, (c) a frozen candidate has PASSED the full rule on DEV_CONFIRM, and (d) a separate, explicit owner HOLDOUT authorisation naming that exact candidate has been issued
holdoutPolicy.isHoldoutOneShot: yes - once per frozen candidate, and at most 3 candidates per HOLDOUT instance (see proposedSplits.multiplicityBudget)
holdoutPolicy.mayTuningFollowAHoldoutFailure: NO tuning against that HOLDOUT, ever. A new candidate returns to DEV_TRAIN and must pass DEV_CONFIRM again before consuming another HOLDOUT budget slot.
holdoutPolicy.doesANewCandidateAfterHoldoutFailureNeed: not while the multiplicity budget of 3 remains; once exhausted, yes - a NEW holdout drawn from organisations never previously used
holdoutPolicy.unchanged: HOLDOUT remains completely inaccessible today. A DEV pass is not a HOLDOUT authorisation. This proposal opens nothing, hashes nothing and enumerates nothing.

rules: 1. Prompt developers may inspect DEV_TRAIN items, documents, labels, rationales and full per-item model outputs, without limit.
2. DEV_CONFIRM and HOLDOUT remain sealed: no item, document, label, per-item result or pre-freeze aggregate may be inspected. Inspecting a DEV_CONFIRM item burns it.
3. Semantic iterations against DEV_TRAIN are unlimited. DEV_CONFIRM scorings are budgeted at 5 per methodology epoch; HOLDOUT scorings at 3 per HOLDOUT instance.
4. A future candidate MAY be designed from known failure items, but only DEV_TRAIN ones. Designing against a DEV_CONFIRM or HOLDOUT item is prohibited and structurally prevented by sealing.
5. A candidate becomes FROZEN when its prompt version, output schema version and request configuration are hashed and committed, before any DEV_CONFIRM provider request.
6. A frozen candidate receives exactly one DEV_CONFIRM evaluation under the stage 0-4 rule.

7. On REJECT: diagnose into the existing classes (A bad gold label, B insufficient evidence, C prompt/rubric ambiguity, D schema/validator issue, E genuine semantic error, F acquisition/page-quality issue), return to DEV_TRAIN, and freeze a new version. Never switch models.
8. On INADMISSIBLE: repair the execution environment and re-run the SAME frozen candidate; this does not consume a budget slot, because nothing about the candidate was measured.
9. Phase 2E becomes eligible only after a HOLDOUT pass under this rule, and Phase 2E entry remains a separate owner decision.
futureCandidateDevelopmentRules.noV7InThisTask: No prompt candidate was created, edited or designed by this task.

machineVerifiableSupport.purity: PURE - no network, no database, no filesystem, no clock, no environment, no Math.random, no Date.now. Randomised procedures take an explicit integer seed.
providedFunctions: clopperPearsonLowerBound - exact one-sided binomial lower confidence bound
minimumTrialsToCertify - the corpus size a threshold needs
maxErrorsUnderPointThreshold - the real integer tolerance of a point gate
gateFeasibility - whether a gate can ever be established at a denominator (the P1 precondition)
passEveryReplicateAcceptanceProbability / requiredPerReplicatePass - the stringency of a must-pass-every-replicate rule
machineVerifiableSupport.notProvided: No scorer for a future candidate is implemented here, deliberately: no candidate exists, and building the scorer now would invite the rule to be shaped around its implementation.

openUnknowns: UNKNOWN: the true label error rate of the existing 49 DEVELOPMENT labels. Never measured; no second annotator, no agreement statistic.

ownerDecisionRequired.decision: approve, amend or reject this methodology BEFORE any future semantic candidate exists
subDecisions: D1. Accept or reject the organisation-disjoint three-split design (the largest structural change).
D2. Accept or reject replacing per-replicate must-pass gating with a clustered lower-confidence-bound gate plus a no-catastrophic-replicate floor.
D3. Choose corpus option A, B or C. This is a cost-versus-ambition decision and is genuinely the owner's, not a technical one.
D4. Confirm whether a second human reviewer is available for dual blind review; if not, ratify UNMEASURED_LABEL_ERROR as a recorded limitation.
D5. Ratify or change the HOLDOUT multiplicity budget of 3.
D6. Resolve d10: name exactly which checks are GATES and which are REPORTING.
ownerDecisionRequired.approvalMustBe: a SEPARATE future record naming this proposal's exact SHA-256. This task does not create it.
